facts.text: A site type is a class of job site with a characteristic layout, surface and traffic, such as an open pit, quarry face, stockpile yard or road works; the "100+ site types" claim means that one machine may work across 100 or more job sites and applications.
facts.quote: A site type is a class of job site with a characteristic layout, surface and traffic (an open pit, a quarry face, a stockpile yard, a road works), and the "100+ site types" claim is the challenge statement that one machine may work across 100 or more job sites and applications.

facts.text: The challenge statement identifies job sites and applications as the first variable that makes validation hard; a literal interpretation would require validation at 100 different places.
facts.quote: The challenge statement lists job sites and applications as the first variable that makes validation hard [Introduction]. Taken literally, that would mean validating on 100 different places.

facts.text: The booklet concludes that a site count is not meaningful until the organization defines whether it counts individually validated sites, parameterized classes of environment or customer configurations inside a validated envelope.
facts.quote: the number is not meaningful until the organization defines what it counts: individually validated sites, parameterized classes of environment, or customer configurations inside a validated envelope [Chapter 13].

facts.text: No standard sets a required number of virtual job sites.
facts.quote: No standard sets a required number of virtual job sites

facts.text: Teams argue that virtual job-site validation is sufficient through coverage of a defined operating domain and its parameters, rather than by counting sites.
facts.quote: teams argue sufficiency through coverage of a defined operating domain and its parameters

facts.text: Two hundred nearly identical dry pit roads provide less validation coverage than a small set of sites spanning different geometry, materials and conditions.
facts.quote: two hundred nearly identical dry pit roads give less coverage than a small set that spans different geometry, materials and conditions [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Site type is one validation parameter alongside surface, slope, object classes, weather and light, machine model and sensor position.
facts.quote: Site type becomes one parameter among many, alongside surface, slope, object classes, weather and light, machine model and sensor position [Chapter 5].

facts.text: The booklet proposes 15 to 30 parameterized site archetypes anchored by 3 to 5 surveyed real sites as one possible starting point, explicitly as planning assumptions rather than evidence.
facts.quote: As planning assumptions rather than evidence, the booklet mentions 15 to 30 parameterized site archetypes anchored by 3 to 5 surveyed real sites as one possible starting point [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Every off-road product found by the booklet launched in a domain much narrower than its full market.
facts.quote: Every off-road product the booklet found launched much narrower than its full market [Chapters 2, 13].

facts.text: The organization's definition of "site type" determines the size of the test space and what can honestly be claimed at release.
facts.quote: How the organization defines "site type" decides the size of the test space and what can honestly be claimed at release.

facts.text: The booklet recommends a library of parameterized representative site types anchored to a few surveyed real sites.
facts.quote: The booklet's advice is a library of parameterized representative site types anchored to a few surveyed real sites

facts.text: The booklet recommends releasing in a narrow operating domain that widens through evidence gates.
facts.quote: with release in a narrow domain that widens by evidence gate [Introduction, Chapters 1, 5].
